'''Alan Kenneth Head''' [[Order of Australia|AO]], [[Australian Academy of Science|FAA]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Humble | first1 = Peter | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2010.0013  | doi-access = free| title = Alan Kenneth Head AO FAA. 10 August 1925 – 9 January 2010 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | year = 2010 | volume = 57 | pages = 147–166 | s2cid = 60657697 }}</ref> (10 August 1925 – 9 January 2010) was an Australian [[physicist]],<ref>[http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/notices-2010/ Notices 2010] Deaths of Fellows in 2010, The Royal Society. Retrieved 26 December 2011.</ref> and Chief of the Division of Chemical Physics, at [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]] from 1981 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Head, Alan Kenneth|url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P000485b.htm|access-date=2020-07-08|website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science|language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Head | first1 = A. K. | author-link = Alan Head| title = A New Form for a Giant Radio Telescope | doi = 10.1038/179692a0 | journal = Nature | volume = 179 | issue = 4562 | pages = 692–693 | year = 1957 | bibcode = 1957Natur.179..692H | s2cid = 41225279 }}</ref>

Head earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] and [[Bachelor of Science]] from the [[University of Melbourne]], [[PhD]] from the [[University of Bristol]], and [[Doctorate of Science]] from the [[University of Melbourne]]. He was made an [[Order of Australia|Officer of the Order of Australia]] in the 1992 Queen's Birthday Honours in recognition of his "service to science through research into the structure of solids and its application to industry".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Alan Kenneth Head|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/885917|access-date=2020-07-09|website=Australian Honours Search Facility, Dept of Prime Minister and Cabinet}}</ref>
